frontier.hypothesis: F28 - the residual is reachable only by splitting the idx[0] chain across calls.c's store_one_arg boundary: the ADDRESS insns (lbu/sll/addu) emitted by the register-arg precompute loop, the final LOAD emitted by load_register_parameters.
frontier.mechanism: Sessions 15's H64 + H66 pin the shape exactly. Target's idx[0] chain is lbu 46 / sll 52 / addu 56 / lw a3 61, spread across the sw 16(sp) at build idx 58. Our four attractors each put the whole chain on ONE side: named-VALUE arg4 puts all four insns before the sw (7 / 91, held there by the REG_DEP_ANTI), fully-inline arg4 puts all four after it (13 / 91), and both the const cast and the named-ADDRESS-with-inline-deref buy the crossing at the cost of the lbu head order (9 / 91). Since the class tie-break is inert and priorities are chassis-invariant, the ONLY thing a C change can move is the pre-sched1 chain order, and calls.c is what sets it.
frontier.next_probe: Read tools/gcc-2.7.2/calls.c 1618-1665 for exactly which expand_expr results are left as MEMs vs forced into pseudos (the TREE_CODE (args[i].tree_value) / args[i].value handling), and expr.c:expand_expr's ARRAY_REF / INDIRECT_REF cases for when the address subexpression is pre-forced into a pseudo. Then look for C that forces the ADDRESS into a pseudo at the statement while leaving the dereference inline in the call - e.g. the index named as a local with the base+deref inline (s32 i0 = idx_1494[0]; ... tbl_125c[i0] ...), or a named pointer with a second use in the block so the precompute loop cannot fold it back. Screen new forms against the rejected bank FIRST (named-index-bytes-inert-vs-pure-inline-13.c and arg3-value-named-12.c are already dead). Screen with sandbox --disable all; confirm any real move with idump.sh + blocksum.py - the presence or absence of the 100->125 REG_DEP_ANTI edge in insn 125's LOG_LINKS is the single readout that says whether the boundary was crossed.

frontier.hypothesis: F23 - the do{}while(0) wrapper is the candidate's single match device and has still never been through a fresh adversarial cheat-reviewer.
frontier.mechanism: It is explicitly sanctioned by the owner's 2026-07-06 do-while(0) ruling (any body, ANY codegen effect, register allocation named explicitly, mandatory inline FAKE annotation, a single level needs no nesting justification) and the candidate carries the annotation. Its only effect is flow.c's loop_depth ref-weighting for the three table pointers; session 12 re-confirmed from calls.c 1653-1664 + stmt.c:2435 + toplev.c:3387 that argument expansion is not loop-gated at -O2, so it has no role in the argument block at all.

frontier.hypothesis: F27 (PROJECT-WIDE, not saEft01Init) - the sandbox-aligned permuter shim is worth keeping for OTHER queue functions, because the stock 100-vs-5 weighting hides register/field-difference signal on any function whose gap is not a clean reordering.
frontier.mechanism: Session 14 measured that the stock objective spends 92% of saEft01Init's base score on two unalignable slots and only 8% on the seven differences the sandbox actually charges for. Any function whose residual is a handful of register/field differences has the same shape, and there the aligned weights are a strictly better gradient - the cross-chassis monotonicity measured there (23<->7, 29<->9) is the property that matters when a campaign is seeded on several chassis. This is an OPERATOR-surface question: making it standard means a knob in tools/permuter_campaign.py, which a grind session may not write.
